item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is materially closer to the frozen contract. It adds the exact requested API and uses the established replayable multipart helper with minimal scope. It still needs a small refactor to delegate to Add and substantially stronger tests.","reasons":["B implements the exact required signature with opts ...FilesOption; A instead invents AddFileOption, breaking the specified API contract.","B directly reuses multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), producing the required replayable bytes.Reader body.","A adds association fields and NewFileWithFields despite the explicit prohibition on adding association fields.","A changes RawClient.Do to buffer every non-replayable request body, an unrelated retry-layer refactor explicitly outside scope. Its makeBodyReplayable also silently ignores source read failures, potentially sending an exhausted or partial body instead of returning the error supplied by the reader contract behavior clarification \"Propagate source-reader failures\" in the Upload contract. More precisely, Upload itself would propagate via NewFileWithFields, but the global Raw path introduced by A does not propagating its own buffering errors, creating dangerous semantics beyond scope; B avoids this machinery entirely. B's NewFile path propagates source-reader failures naturally, although it lacks a test for this behavior. B's validation is present and prevents requests on empty filename or nil content, though tests do not verify it. Neither candidate routes Upload through FilesService.Add as required; both duplicate Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data check. B's violation is localized and straightforward to fix by calling Add, while A compounds it with a second option system and multipart extension. B's retry test confirms bytes.Reader bodies are replayable, but does not test Upload end-to-end from a streamed reader. Its multipart test checks field and filename but fails to assert uploaded content. A has better multipart-content and validation assertions, yet these do not outweigh its direct API and scope violations."],"risks_a":["Public Upload signature violates the exact contract and makes existing FilesOption values unusable.","Forbidden association APIs and multipart-field machinery create unnecessary public surface and maintenance burden.","Global RawClient buffering changes semantics and memory use for all reader-backed requests, not just uploads, and may silently consume a failing reader before sending a damaged request body rather than report the read failure. This is especially risky because makeBodyReplayable returns no error and ignores io.ReadAll errors. It also buffers direct Files.Add bodies globally, contrary to preserving the lower-level API's existing behavior/scope intent. The Add retry test passes a raw application/octet-stream body rather than validating the custom multipart use case described for Add. Upload still bypasses Add, so future Add behavior can drift."],"risks_b":["Upload duplicates Add instead of delegating to it, violating the explicit single-path requirement and risking future divergence.","Multipart test never reads or checks the file content.","No tests cover validation, source-reader errors, FilesOption forwarding, or an end-to-end retry of Upload with streamed content. The generic bytes.Reader transport test does not fully satisfy the streamed-content retry requirement. Lack of a doc comment on the exported Upload method is less idiomatic for Go public API."]}
